title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: improve visibility and correctness of burst utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets and add a SLO-based fallback that prevents aggressive autoscale bursts from violating throughput guarantees. This PR updates the autoscaler token-bucket smoothing, adds per-fleet and per-priority utilization metrics, fixes an edge case in the burst allowance calc when previous-window utilization is noisy, and exposes a CLI flag to simulate burst throttles for QA.

Changes: checklist: - [x] Implement token-bucket smoothing tweak and deterministic decay (autoscaler/core/tokenbucket.go) - [x] Add new Prometheus metrics (observability/metrics/dedicated_metrics.go): dedicated_burst_allowed_tokens, dedicated_burst_tokens_consumed, dedicated_fleet_utilization_5m, dedicated_fleet_utilization_1h, dedicated_priority_throttle_events - [x] Emit utilization percentiles used by console reporting (50/90/99) - [x] Add config for SLO-fallback thresholds and graceful shedding policy (config/dedicated_autoscaler.yaml) - [x] Add unit and integration tests covering edgecases and race conditions - [x] Update docs and release notes

Description: The autoscaler previously relied on a simple moving average over a fixed window which could be skewed by intermittent large jobs (cold-starts or large-batch retries) and cause the token-bucket to allow large bursts that later starved lower-priority workloads. This change switches smoothing to an exponential decay tuned to our observed request distributions and introduces a carryover cap so burst allowances never exceed a configurable multiple of the steady-state capacity. We also record more granular utilization metrics per-fleet and per-priority so the Console can show both short (5m) and long (1h) utilization trends and correlate throttle events with downstream errors. Finally, we add an SLO-fallback policy: if the 1h utilization exceeds the SLO threshold for a fleet, the autoscaler enters a conservative mode where bursts are limited and lower-priority queues are shed gradually instead of allowing immediate large token consumption.

Testing and rollout: unit tests added for token-bucket math and smoothing edgecases. Integration test harness simulates mixed priority traffic with bursty patterns and asserts throughput guarantees for high-priority routes. CI initially failed on a flaky test (TestTokenBucketRace) which was hardened and re-run; all checks pass. We will rollout to staging with feature flag gaussian_autoscale_smoothing disabled, enable in canary for two small fleets for 48 hours, then enable broadly pending metrics verification.

Related: ENG-2784 (autoscaler improvements), SUP-4421 (customer reported burst outage), design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2784/dedicated-autoscaler-smoothing-and-util-reporting

Notes for reviewers: focus on tokenbucket.go correctness, metric cardinality, and SLO-fallback policy (config knobs and default thresholds).

release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler smoothing and utilization reporting: more stable burst controls, SLO-fallback policy to prevent throughput regressions, new metrics for per-fleet and per-priority utilization, and a QA CLI to simulate burst throttles.
changelog_entry: Autoscaler: better burst smoothing and utilization metrics (ENG-2784).
backcompat_risks: Low: adds new metrics and a conservative default for SLO-fallback; feature is behind a flag and defaults preserve previous behavior.
qa_instructions: Enable feature flag 'gaussian_autoscale_smoothing' in staging. Use cli/commands/simulate_burst.go to run synthetic mixed-priority traffic for 30 minutes. Verify dedicated_fleet_utilization_5m and dedicated_priority_throttle_events counters and confirm high-priority throughput remains within target SLO.
notes: This PR was driven by SUP-4421 customer incident where aggressive bursts caused transient retries. The SLO-fallback ensures graceful degradation and improves observability to diagnose future incidents.
